articles.title: India earns nearly 50% more from fuel exports in April-September as costlier oil and weak rupee outweigh lower volumes
articles.titleEn: India earns nearly 50% more from fuel exports in April-September as costlier oil and weak rupee outweigh lower volumes
articles.summary: India's petroleum product export earnings increased significantly in April to September, driven by high international prices. While the volume of shipments declined by 16%, earnings surged by nearly 50% in rupee terms. Diesel exports were the largest contributors to the earnings growth, accounting for 42% of the total volume. Both diesel and petrol consumption rose during this period, whereas production saw slight declines.
